trial_court: Senior Civil Judge, Tanuku (HMOP No.235 of 2018)
case_name: Burra Venkata Niranjan vs Burra Somidevi Kanthiranjani
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed HMOP for divorce. Respondent sought maintenance and legal expenses. Trial Court granted Rs.10,000/- towards maintenance. Petitioner challenged the order.

legal_principles.principle: The trial court ought not to have compelled the parties to pay maintenance in a certain manner despite defense on the record, which is not sustainable under law and liable to be remitted to the Court for fresh consideration basing on its own merits.
legal_principles.held: The trial Court ought not to have compelled the parties to pay certain manner despite defense on the record, which is not sustainable under law and liable to be remitted to the Court for fresh consideration basing on his defense on its own merits, else prejudice would be caused to the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: The trial court ought to have considered the counter filed by the petitioner admitting that his salary is only Rs.24,000/- but not Rs.30,000/- as mentioned in the Order.
legal_principles.held: The trial Court failed to consider the Counter filed by the petitioner to the application filed under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order is contrary to law, weight of evidence, and probabilities of the case. The matter is remitted to the trial court for fresh consideration.
